title: The $\ell$-adic Tate module is free of rank $2g$
statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety ([def-sc-abelian-variety]) of dimension $g$ over an algebraically
closed field $k$ and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Then

$$
T_\ell A\cong\Z_\ell^{2g},\qquad V_\ell A\cong\Q_\ell^{2g}.
$$

proof.text: Put $M=A(k)$. Since [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective] gives surjectivity of $[n]:A(k)\to A(k)$ for every $n\ge 1$, multiplication by $\ell$ on $M$ is surjective. Applying [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale] with $n=\ell$ (allowed because $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$) and using the kernel definition identifies $M[\ell]$ with $A[\ell](k)\cong(\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z)^{2g}$, so $\operatorname{Nat.card}(M[\ell])=\ell^{2g}$. The hypotheses of [lem-av-tate-module-group-rank] therefore give a linear equivalence $T_\ell M\simeq (\mathbf Z_\ell)^{2g}$; by [def-wf-abelian-tate-module], $T_\ell M$ is the module denoted $T_\ell A$. The rational conclusion follows from [lem-av-rational-tate-module-group-rank] with the same divisibility and cardinality hypotheses, giving $V_\ell A\simeq (\mathbf Q_\ell)^{2g}$.
